notes: No page on woodenstreet.com is named/breadcrumbed Clearance, Outlet, Final Sale, Last Chance, or End of Line (categories.xml, 1684 URLs, has zero matches for clear/outlet; direct probes to /clearance, /clearance-sale, /outlet, /outlet-sale, /clearance-furniture, /end-of-line, /last-chance all 404). One ambiguous candidate was found and is recorded below rather than silently dropped: https://www.woodenstreet.com/furniture-sale. Its own breadcrumb reads 'Furniture sale' and its H1 reads 'Furniture Sale' (a generic-sale label, not a strict clearance word) - BUT its SEO <title> tag literally reads 'Furniture Sale: Clearance Deals Up to 70% Off - Shop Now!', explicitly using the word Clearance. Working against permanence: this hub's own children (found via parent_key/breadcrumb linkage) are all festival/day-specific temporary campaigns - Diwali Offer (149 products, parent_key=furniture-sale), Festive Sale (106, parent_key=furniture-sale), Father's Day Sale (124), Gudi Padwa Sale (found in categories.xml) - and Deal of the Day (643 products, breadcrumb 'Furniture sale > Deal of the day'), a rotating daily-discount page. This pattern (rotating festival/day campaigns nested under one 'Sale' hub, with 'Clearance' appearing only in marketing SEO copy, not the breadcrumb/H1) reads more like a generic temporary promotional sale than a genuine permanent outlet/clearance listing, but the explicit title-tag use of 'Clearance' keeps it genuinely ambiguous rather than a confident exclude - flagged per brief instead of guessing. The festival/day-named children themselves (Diwali Offer, Festive Sale, Father's Day Sale, Gudi Padwa Sale, Deal of the Day) are NOT recorded as rows - they are unambiguously temporary seasonal/promotional campaigns with no clearance/outlet signal of their own, so excluded outright rather than flagged. Access: direct HTTP fetch throughout, no block, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow.
